findings.design: A shared private-group/private-root predicate fixes readers and writers. Build from a pristine pinned export. Retain the established source-before-install orchestration but automatically restore the durable backup on pre-publication failure; the previous managed release stays active. This smaller complete transaction preserves existing installer/pipx ownership APIs. It does not claim the checkout moves only after publication. World-write remains rejected even beneath a private root.
findings.evidence: Actual managed + pipx install/update/overwrite/revert/re-recovery under umask 002 passed all 33 checks; private-group and private-root unit regressions; automatic failed-build source restoration regression.

findings.design: Aggregate bounded source/destination diagnostics provide one quoted chmod hint. A prohibited ancestor can still prevent deeper inspection, which remains fail-closed. No recursive permission changes are performed.
findings.evidence: The real umask002 lifecycle succeeds; legacy source-only markers inside a private release are covered; source_snapshot runs during --plan; bootstrap local-root detection reports trust failure instead of silently choosing another checkout.

findings.design: Use the existing shared predicate at write boundaries rather than independently repairing permissions after writing.
findings.evidence: The setup suite passed 16 cases; configuration/trust and state-preflight tests pass. Writers use directory_fd; temporary setup JSON uses explicit 0600 creation; state errors identify the exact parent and chmod command. Final integration: 121 project-picker+migration tests pass; ENOTDIR/ELOOP migration refusal retains the documented ValueError and proves no output or source mutation.

findings.design: Managed builds use a private git archive; pipx builds a wheel in a disposable standard-library venv and installs through the owning pipx manager. This supports pip- and uv-backed pipx without building in the source checkout. Modern pipx's rewritten source field is restored atomically while preserving refreshed metadata.
findings.evidence: Actual installed imports prove a deleted module is absent and a package-to-module replacement imports the new module even with stale build/lib files planted. Pristine source and installed RECORD/wheel package inventories are compared. A tracked module hidden by export-ignore is rejected against pinned git ls-tree rather than silently omitted.
findings.resolution: implemented for managed and pipx installations

findings.design: Use Git's own bounded threading configuration and one retry. Bootstrap drains stderr with selectors and retains only a redacted tail; updater reuses raven.redaction.
findings.evidence: Both bootstrap suites assert pack.threads/index.threads/fetch.parallel/checkout.workers=1 and depth=1; fetch and clone retry once. Stderr is bounded and scrubbed; actual shallow bootstrap cloning runs in installed lifecycle qualification.

findings.design: Send catchable SIGTERM first, allow up to ten seconds of leader cleanup, and retain the leader's PID with WNOWAIT until final process-group cleanup. No blind stale-lock deletion.
findings.evidence: Existing owned-process interruption/timeout/descendant assertions remain passing. Git reset/fetch have a separate 600-second mutation timeout; metadata has a 60-second bound. Stale index.lock errors name the exact path and inspection/removal remedy.

findings.design: Move the Python heredoc out of command substitution; safely expand an empty Bash array. CI builds and executes the actual interpreter versions instead of approximating their parser behavior.
findings.evidence: Reproducible SHA-pinned GNU Bash 3.2 and 4.2 builders each passed all 41 bootstrap cases. Sources and commands are recorded in /workspace/review-bash-helper-32-2/result.json and /workspace/review-bash-helper-42-2/result.json.
findings.resolution: implemented and executed on both legacy interpreters

findings.design: Interpreter isolation removes the calling directory before any standard-library imports; no PYTHONPATH cleanup heuristic is needed.
findings.evidence: A planted random.py in the calling directory does not execute during bootstrap. Python probes, temporary-file helpers, and bootstrap execution use -I.
Root owns the shared COL-8/COL-13/INS-9 transport fix and its qualification; this package makes no independent passing claim.
findings.resolution: delegated to root shared SSH transport package

findings.design: Prune only completed, checksum-matching Raven backups and marker-owned releases under maintenance/install locks. Preserve three latest recovery points and explicitly selected ones, plus their referenced interpreters. Delete refs with their expected old commit, preserving concurrently changed refs.
findings.evidence: Regression creates five complete backups and proves exactly three corresponding backups/refs survive. Stable worker interpreter regression verifies current/bin/python. Actual update/revert/re-recovery succeeds.

findings.design: Bounded 128-descriptor parent-fd LRU; no per-file root walk; each populated directory is synced once. Eliminate the duplicate pre-mutation verification, while preserving a complete byte check immediately before mutation. Traced times include instrumentation overhead and are not NFS speed claims. Normal CPU/RSS/I/O evidence was collected in the coordinated quiet final window; process RSS and Python allocations are explicitly distinguished.
findings.evidence: Equivalent 2,672-file local warm fixtures: selected syscall total 369071 to 87298, openat 155604 to 26406, fstat 173278 to 28482, fsync 5416 to 2745. Traced wall time 33.60s to 8.78s. Raw data: /workspace/review-install-perf/{baseline,current}{.json,-strace.txt}. Quiet normal wall 5.336s to 2.763s; user CPU 1.398s to .363s; system CPU 1.346s to .939s; process max RSS 18096 to 17648 KiB; output 24568 to 24560 Linux 512-byte blocks. Identical 2672-file payload SHA256 18ca8d92f963814c7df36d31d0d63904e7532a7b61967fda08403f73c1597696. Full consolidated evidence /workspace/review-install-benchmark.json. findings.design: Ordinary main commits do not necessarily have release artifacts: the existing workflow attests tags/manual release candidates. Requiring nonexistent attestations by default would break ordinary updates. Default requires every declared and effective fetch URL to identify the official repository, immutable fetched commit and printed exact range; forks require explicit authorization. --require-attestation fails closed using the existing GitHub/Sigstore signer policy. Local checksums are never described as authentication.
findings.evidence: Tests reject fork updates without --allow-fork, reject missing/failed required attestations before checkout mutation, and assert exact source/signer digests and workflow identity in gh arguments. Build tools pin setuptools 84.0.0 and wheel 0.48.0. Final independent review additionally reproduced declared/effective URL disagreement and fixed every effective fetch URL check. Official SSH rewrite, actual redirected local update refusal/fork recovery, all-URL checks and credential-free diagnostics pass in the final 105-case trust/update run and 236 coordinator checks.
findings.qualification_limit: A successful live verifier run for the delivered commit requires its published attested artifact and GitHub verifier access. Unit verifier success is simulated and labeled as such.
findings.resolution: implemented authorized-source default plus explicit fail-closed attestation policy

findings.design: Apply build-input visibility rules before mutation rather than relying only on gitignore-aware status. Bounded exact git clean paths avoid deleting ignored user data.
findings.evidence: A git-info/exclude-hidden raven/helper.py is reported as a local executable change; normal update refuses, overwrite removes that exact ignored executable input, and adjacent ignored scientific data remains intact.

findings.design: Sweep at most 256 candidates under a private maintenance lock after one hour, requiring Raven's ownership marker and a nonexistent recorded PID. Legacy markerless trees lack sufficient ownership evidence and remain untouched; a user must review them before manual cleanup. This conservative adjustment avoids deleting unrelated or still-active environments.
findings.evidence: HUP and QUIT use the same owned-process cancellation path as TERM/INT. Stage sweep tests remove a private marker-bearing dead-process stage while preserving a live stage and an unknown unmarked directory.
findings.resolution: implemented signal cleanup and provable stale-stage sweeping

findings.design: Keep implicit default bootstrap creation convenient while making explicit destination creation deliberate.
findings.evidence: Bootstrap tests cover explicit source paths and cloning. Explicit missing --source-dir now fails unless --clone is supplied, with a case-insensitive sibling spelling hint.
Piped bootstrap uses the declared default/explicit source and never adopts an incidental current-directory checkout; only an existing named install.sh file enables local auto-discovery.
Bootstrap probes python3.14 down through python3.10 before python3/python; explicit --python still takes precedence. All probes use isolated mode.

findings.design: Verify the staged installed environment rather than accepting a checkout import that can conceal missing wheel contents.
findings.evidence: Actual managed installation passes python -I import checks from the stage cwd, asserts raven.__file__ is inside sys.prefix and checks installed package RECORD against pristine inputs.

findings.design: Mutable state requires verified local storage; durable allocation receipts receive path trust checks without incorrectly imposing a node-local filesystem requirement. Managed SSH's early-return path also retains local state preflight.
findings.evidence: Both doctors call shared read-only trust/filesystem/state preflight on effective paths. Tests verify no store creation and precise offending-parent diagnostics. Heavy owner confirmed launcher doctor prints the complete JSON evidence, so state/receipt warnings are visible.

Source roots are expanded and resolved before comparison; root-symlink/relative-segment tests preserve canonical identity. Post-publication failures re-read current and report the real selected release instead of claiming the previous release remains active.

findings.design: raven trust PATH delegates configuration/code authority to the reviewed shared root owners/group without chmod or mandatory-policy bypass. Grants bind uid/device/inode and are stored atomically in private configuration under a serialized lock. Real PI-owned cluster deployment remains unqualified on this single-user host.
findings.evidence: Private-group identity matrix, private 0700 shielding, PI-owner predicate fixtures, bounded private registry, replaced-inode revocation, root grant removal, and no-follow-inside-root tests pass. Selected XDG roots resolve once while internal symlinks remain rejected. Mandatory site policy rejects group write even when a private-group exception would otherwise apply. Final plugin-root review additionally verifies an explicitly selected plugin-directory alias resolves once while internal/final symlinks and writable roots remain refused; retargeting the selected alias after discovery does not redirect execution.
findings.resolution: implemented shared trust and explicit root grants

maintenance_review.package_boundary: Canonical code lives under raven/installation with exact legacy sys.modules aliases. Standalone installer trust loader keeps its original location and installed command dispatch retains original import paths.

maintenance_review.simpler_alternatives_rejected: Blind chmod, deleting unknown stages, deleting build/ in the user's checkout, trusting arbitrary remotes, skipping failed provenance verification, and dropping pre-mutation fidelity checks were rejected in favor of narrowly owned operations.
